Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Is sertraline the same as Zoloft?
:
Yes.
Sertraline is the active ingredient.
Zoloft is the brand name it is sold under in the United States.
Sertraline is the generic version of Zoloft.
The two contain the same medicine, sertraline hydrochloride.
You may also see it written as sertraline HCl.
Is sertraline an SSRI, and how does it work?
:
Yes, sertraline is an SSRI, which stands for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.
Nerve cells in the brain release serotonin to send signals.
Then, they reabsorb it.
Sertraline blocks that reabsorption.
More serotonin stays available between nerve cells.
Sertraline has very little effect on norepinephrine.
Sertraline has very little effect on dopamine.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on adrenergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on cholinergic receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on GABA receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on histamine receptors.
Sertraline has no meaningful effect on benzodiazepine receptors.
This lack of effect on multiple receptors is part of why sertraline is described as selective.
Triplet: ["sertraline", "has no meaningful effect on", "adrenergic receptors"]

The relation 'has no meaningful effect on' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug does not significantly interact with or influence the receptor or system specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. B. 'not chemically related to': The subject drug does not share a chemical structure or mechanism of action with the substance specified by the object entity.
C. 'has no interaction with': The subject drug does not have a known interaction with the object entity.
D. 'is not considered addictive in the way': The subject drug is not considered addictive in the manner or to the extent of the substance specified by the object entity.
E. 'not used for': The subject drug is not indicated or used to treat or manage the condition or situation specified by the object entity.
